questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Safety in the host country
- Academic level at host university 
- Level of English in host university and in host country 
- Infrastructure of host country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was not that easy; however, it was pretty manageable after some time. 
To me, it was helpful that I could communicate in my own language, as all Norwegians do not speak English.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance in finding the student accommodation - however all assistance stops here. No help getting there, finding out how to get into the laundry room etc. The university "welcome day" was done in Norweigian entirely.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: This information was provided by the university and ucph abroad.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It takes time to get to the city center. If you can choose housing available in Fantoft. There you will have the most exchange students and facilities available. Block F is definetly the best block to live in. You have one roommate and approximately 14 other flatmates, who you are a big and nice kitchen and common area with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was fairly easy - just had many administrative steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much help was available - however they were very kind to attempt at helping at the student center.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I enrolled in all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
- Please read the courses through thouroly and make sure the don't overlap. 
- Most of the exams will be closed book, school exams with no means of help. This means memorizing a lot of PowerPoints.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: BA and MA courses were merged together. The only difference was the amount of reading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different - and a lot less interactive. You may have some reading to do before class, but it is the professor who speaks for two hours and then you leave.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Law of the Sea
2. Competition Law
3. Law, Regulation and Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Competition Law was very giving. It is a fun course, and the teaching structure is similar to courses provided at KU.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Money spent on spontaneous hiking trips etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is very expensive - and living in Norway is, in general, a lot more expensive than first anticipated. 
Be prepared.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Hiking clubs, football, and running clubs. 
Club Fantoft had parties and other events from time to time.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking definetly! Being out in nature and taking in the sights makes you feel more calm and at peace. I would recommend 10/10. Go to Tromsø, Nordkapp, Lofoten - all of it! You will have the experience of a lifetime.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Tromsø, Nordkapp, Lofoten - all of it! You will have the experience of a lifetime. Do the 7 mountains hike in Bergen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very similar to danish, so for me personally - it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Drinking and hiking are a big part of the local students' culture - you should be somewhat willing to at least participate in these activities (you can always drink soda).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The drinking culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Learn to take things easy and go with the flow. 
2. Bring all the stuff you need with you. 
3. Enjoy it! Time goes by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going to Tromsø, Nordkapp, Lofoten - all of it! Going there with all of my 14 flatmates for a two-week trip made the experience of a lifetime - and friends from all over Europe for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say having a lot of freetime.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
